digest.component_or_area: code-review gate model-class wiring and LLM usage logging
propositions: The code-review gate silently ignores the per-step model class declarations in code-review.yaml and runs every LLM pass on the single resolved cfg.model.
The defect is pre-existing (verify has declared model: standard since story 172e) and confirmed by hypothesis H1: the step's declared model never reaches resolve_model.

usage_log.record() records only the prompt name (op) and cannot attribute a call to a step, so base cannot be distinguished from the round_a/round_b batch finder which share the code-review-base prompt.

Step 0 adds a ContextVar carrying the step id and raw declared class token from the executor to runner.py:547, so record() can additively write step and model_class (only when the token is in CLASS_NAMES).

An offline end-to-end recording-runner test must sit beneath the production RunnerAgentStep and assert each of the five steps (base, round_a, round_b, verify, coach) receives its declared class under a class table differing from cfg.model, observed RED before the fix.

Plan-review honors classes because it wraps run_workflow in gate_config(cfg) while the code-review dispatch path omits it; the actual broken seam is one of gate_dispatch, runs, or batch_runner and must be identified before fixing without changing any declaration.
